title: Multi-agent system architecture and orchestration
subtitle: A governance control plane, a persona-driven runtime and a voice-first collaboration shell: three ways I have organised many agents around one body of work, with the state outside any model's head.
lede: Governance, a runtime and collaboration: each time, I treated many agents as a distributed system held to the accountability I expect from people, with explicit state, separated duties, traceable messages and failure domains drawn on purpose. AgentOS started from a diagnosis: long agent runs drift because the lead agent has to hold every teammate's state in its head, and past some horizon it forgets one. I moved team state into a PostgreSQL work graph. Seats from more than one vendor run in containers on more than one machine under one contract, emit signed events and carry cost per seat, and adding a vendor means adding an adapter to that contract.
quote: Team state lives in a database, because an agent that must remember everyone's status eventually forgets one.
evidence: Agent orchestration: team state for long agent runs moved into a PostgreSQL work graph, with each seat given a small, freshly rendered job.
Separation of duties for AI work: separate builder and checker seats, an adversarial seat on a different vendor's model and a gatekeeper that judges only what was delivered.
Multi-agent collaboration systems: signed agent messages that carry their call chain and refuse delegation loops, and a council where models deliberate and ratify a decision.
author: Corey James
